questions.question: In a game with $n$ players, player $i$ has a privately known type $\theta_i\in\Theta_i$ and $\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$. What does the common prior assumption require about the players' beliefs over $\Theta$?
options: Each player $i$ has her own distribution $p_i$ on $\Theta$, and each $p_i$ is known only to player $i$.
Every $\theta_i$ is drawn from the same distribution on a type set shared by all players.
Every player observes the realized profile $\theta$, so the distribution $p$ is known to all.
One distribution $p$ on $\Theta$ is common knowledge; each type's belief is $p$ conditioned on her type.

questions.question: In a game with $n$ players, player $i$ has a privately known type $\theta_i\in\Theta_i$ and $\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$. Every player knows the common prior $p$ on $\Theta$. Why does the assumption also require $p$ to be common knowledge?
options: So each player can compute her own belief $p(\theta_{-i}\mid\theta_i)$ from her type and the prior $p$.
So each player can deduce the realized types of the other players from the prior $p$.
So the conditional beliefs $p(\theta_{-i}\mid\theta_i)$ of each type sum to one over $\theta_{-i}$.
So each player can reason about the others' beliefs, including those about her.

questions.question: In a game with $n$ players, player $i$ has a privately known type $\theta_i\in\Theta_i$ and $\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$. The common prior is independent across players, $p(\theta)=\prod_j p_j(\theta_j)$, and every type has positive probability. How does the belief of type $\theta_i$ about $\theta_{-i}$ depend on $\theta_i$?
options: It is the same for every type of $i$: the product of the others' marginals.
It differs across types of player $i$, because each type conditions on her own $\theta_i$.
It equals player $i$'s own marginal $p_i$, applied to the other players' types.
It puts probability one on the others having types equal to $\theta_i$ itself.

questions.question: In a game with $n$ players, player $i$ has a privately known type $\theta_i\in\Theta_i$ and $\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$. Under a common prior $p$, type $\theta_i$ believes $p(\theta_{-i}\mid\theta_i)=p(\theta_i,\theta_{-i})\big/\sum_{\theta'_{-i}}p(\theta_i,\theta'_{-i})$. What does the denominator equal?
options: The marginal probability $p(\theta_{-i})$ that the others have the types $\theta_{-i}$.
The marginal probability $p(\theta_i)$ that player $i$ has type $\theta_i$.
The total probability $1$, since $p$ is a probability distribution on $\Theta$.
The number of type profiles $\theta'_{-i}$ that the other players can have.

questions.question: In a game with $n$ players, player $i$ has a privately known type $\theta_i\in\Theta_i$ and $\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$. The belief of type $\theta_i$ is defined as $p(\theta_{-i}\mid\theta_i)$ under the condition $p(\theta_i)>0$. What does this condition require?
options: Only that $\theta_i$ has positive marginal probability, not each profile with it.
That every profile $(\theta_i,\theta_{-i})$ containing type $\theta_i$ has positive probability.
That every type $\theta_{-i}$ of the other players has positive marginal probability.
That type $\theta_i$ is more likely than each of the other types in $\Theta_i$.

questions.question: Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. The prior is $p(a,x)=0.3$, $p(a,y)=0.2$, $p(b,x)=0.1$, $p(b,y)=0.4$. What probability does type $a$ of player 1 assign to player 2 being of type $x$?

Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. The prior is $p(a,x)=0.12$, $p(a,y)=0.28$, $p(b,x)=0.18$, $p(b,y)=0.42$. What probabilities do types $a$ and $b$ of player 1 assign to player 2 being of type $x$?

Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. Type $a$ has prior probability $p(a)=0.6$ and believes player 2 is of type $x$ with probability $0.25$. What prior probability does the profile $(a,x)$ have?

Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. The prior is $p(a,x)=0.1$, $p(a,y)=0.3$, $p(b,x)=0.5$, $p(b,y)=0.1$. For a fixed action profile, type $a$ of player 1 gets payoff $6$ if player 2 is of type $x$ and $-3$ if of type $y$. What is type $a$'s expected payoff?

Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. Types are independent, with $p(a)=0.3$ for player 1 and $p(x)=0.8$ for player 2. What prior probability does the profile $(b,y)$ have?

Two players have no private information (each has a single possible type). Player 1 assigns probability $0.3$ and player 2 probability $0.6$ to the event that it rains tomorrow. Can these beliefs be derived from a common prior?
options: Yes: a prior that gives rain probability $0.45$, the average of the two, will do.
Yes: a common prior restricts the beliefs only of players who have private information.
Yes, provided neither player knows the other's belief, so the disagreement stays private.
No: without private information both beliefs equal the prior's probability of rain.

questions.question: Under a common prior, players 1 and 2 have different private information and posterior probabilities $q_1$ and $q_2$ of the same event $E$. Which claim about $q_1$ and $q_2$ is correct?
options: They must be equal, since both are derived from the same prior distribution.
They may differ even when both values are common knowledge, since the information differs.
They may differ, but not if both values are common knowledge between the players.
They must both equal the prior probability $p(E)$, since conditioning preserves the prior.

questions.question: Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. All four types have positive probability, and both types of player 1 assign the same probability distribution to $\theta_2$. What follows for player 2's beliefs about $\theta_1$?
options: Nothing: the types of player 2 may still hold different beliefs about $\theta_1$.
Player 2's types must both believe that $a$ and $b$ are equally likely.
Player 2's types share one belief, as $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ are then independent.
Player 2's types must hold player 1's belief about $\theta_2$ as their belief about $\theta_1$.

questions.question: Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. Type $a$ has $p(a)=0.4$ and type $b$ has $p(b)=0.6$; player 2 has $p(x)=0.7$, $p(y)=0.3$. For a fixed plan of player 1, type $a$'s expected payoff is $5$ and type $b$'s is $2$. What is player 1's ex ante expected payoff?

Three players each have type $H$ or $L$; the common prior on $(\theta_1,\theta_2,\theta_3)$ is $p(HHH)=0.24$, $p(HHL)=p(HLH)=0.08$, $p(HLL)=0.20$ and $0.10$ for each of the four profiles with $\theta_1=L$. What probability does type $H$ of player 1 assign to $\theta_2=\theta_3=H$?

Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. Player 1 has $p(a)=0.4$; type $a$ believes $\theta_2=x$ with probability $0.5$ and type $b$ with probability $0.2$. What probability does type $x$ of player 2 assign to player 1 being of type $a$?

Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$. Only player 1's beliefs are specified: type $a$ assigns probability $0.6$ and type $b$ probability $0.2$ to $\theta_2=x$. Which statement about common priors $p$ with $p(a)>0$ and $p(b)>0$ that generate these two beliefs is correct?
options: Every value $p(a)\in(0,1)$ yields such a prior, so these beliefs do not pin $p$ down.
No such prior exists, since under a common prior both types must hold the same belief.
Exactly one such prior exists: the one with $p(a)=p(b)=\tfrac{1}{2}$ for player 1's types.
Such a prior exists only if player 2's two types also agree in their beliefs about $\theta_1$.

questions.question: In a game with $n$ players, player $i$ has a privately known type $\theta_i\in\Theta_i$ and $\Theta=\Theta_1\times\cdots\times\Theta_n$. An analyst computes every type's expected payoff with the marginal $p(\theta_{-i})$ instead of $p(\theta_{-i}\mid\theta_i)$. When does this give the right answer for every payoff function and every type with $p(\theta_i)>0$?
options: Exactly when $\theta_i$ is independent of $\theta_{-i}$ under $p$.
Exactly when $p$ is the uniform distribution on $\Theta$.
Exactly when the types of the other players are independent of each other.
Exactly when every player's type has the same marginal distribution.

questions.question: Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. Type $a$ believes $x$ with probability $0.6$, type $b$ believes $x$ with probability $0.2$, and type $x$ believes $a$ with probability $0.75$. Both of player 1's types have positive probability. What must type $y$ believe about $a$?

Players 1 and 2 privately know their types $\theta_1\in\{a,b\}$ and $\theta_2\in\{x,y\}$, and beliefs come from a common prior $p$. The prior is $p(a,x)=p(a,y)=0.5$ and $p(b,x)=p(b,y)=0$. Which statement about the beliefs derived from $p$ is correct?
options: Types $x$ and $y$ assign probability $1$ to $a$; type $b$ assigns probability $0$ to $x$.
Types $x$ and $y$ assign probability $1/2$ to $a$; type $b$ gets no belief.
Type $x$ gets no belief because $p(b,x)=0$; type $a$ assigns probability $1/2$ to $x$.
Types $x$ and $y$ assign probability $1$ to $a$; the formula gives type $b$ no belief.
